messages:
nina (Sales): Heads-up — Zenith moving from POC -> commit. Need capacity plan + pricing delta. They expect 1200 qps peak (short bursts), ~200 qps sustained, mix = chat(70%)/embeddings(30%). Also flagged: KMS, VPC peering, AZ affinity, and a 2hr prewarm window before daily peak. Can SE + infra confirm reserved GPUs, autoscale policy, and burst behavior?
Ben (Solutions): Quick clarifying q: 1200 qps is requests/sec or inference calls/sec? avg tokens per call? latency SLO?
nina (Sales): 1200 requests/sec at peak. Typical chat request ~300 tokens in, 400 tokens out avg. Latency SLO p95 <= 600ms, p50 target 120-200ms.
Ben (Solutions): Ok. Back-of-envelope: 1200 req/s * 700 tokens ~ 840k tokens/sec. With quantized Llama-ish model at ~50k tokens/s/GPU (in our profile for short seq), that's ~17 GPU-equivalents peak. But batching and KV cache reduce needs for chat flows.
Ben (Solutions): My recommendation: Dedicated reserved pool sized for baseline sustained load + buffer for bursts. Proposed baseline = support 200 qps sustained -> ~4 GPUs. For 1200 qps peak -> autoscale up to ~18 GPUs. We'll suggest reservation commit for 6-8 GPUs and burst credits configured for autoscale above that.
Olivia (SRE): Agree with approach. Notes: KV cache warmup matters for first requests after scale-up. Prewarm window (2h) will reduce burst startup cost. Suggest autoscale policy with prewarm + gradual steps to avoid cold-cache thrash.
Olivia (SRE): Example autoscale policy snippet:
```yaml
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 2
  reserved_replicas: 6   # commit-reserved GPUs
  target_qps_per_gpu: 200
  max_replicas: 20
  scale_up_step: 2
  scale_down_after: 300  # seconds
  prewarm_seconds: 7200
```
Tim (Infra): For pricing: Reserved commit (6 GPUs) + burst usage priced as GPU-hour at on-demand rate * 1.1 for overage. If they take 8 reserved GPUs we can tighten overage multiplier. I'll pull exact $ numbers for A100-equivalent but ballpark: reserved monthly vs on-demand gives ~40% savings.
Tim (Infra): Also check AZ affinity: we can pin reserved pool to 2 AZs for locality, but cross-AZ fallback is automatic. Need to confirm if customer requires strict AZ affinity for compliance.
Ben (Solutions): On the throughput math: with batching improvements + prefix cache we commonly see effective tokens/sec per GPU improve by ~1.5x during steady-state chat. So planned max_replicas 20 gives headroom. Also recommend route-level throttles for embeddings-heavy endpoints to protect latency-sensitive chat routes.
nina (Sales): Customer legal asked for runbook/operational checklist for commit handoff and security Q answers. Can we produce quick bulleted doc they can attach to contract? Key asks: SOC2, KMS integration, data deletion window, VPC peering, logs retention.
Olivia (SRE): Will do. Quick answers inline: SOC2 scope: platform + control plane (we provide attestation). KMS: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM, integration required before private deployment. VPC peering: supported for Dedicated/Private. Data retention: default 30 days; enterprise can request custom retention and audit logs.
Ben (Solutions): I'll draft the runbook sections: capacity sizing assumptions, autoscale snippet, prewarm schedule, fallback plan (model-variant fallback to smaller quantized model), pricing table (reserve vs burst), and contact matrix.
Tim (Infra): Action item for pricing ops: create two quotes — (A) 6-GPU commit + burst credits, (B) 8-GPU commit with lower overage rate. Include cost-per-embedding unit and per-1k-token generation delta.
Ben (Solutions): Suggest we include a simple throttling rule to enforce steady-state: 
`/v1/chat` route -> soft limit 300 qps per route, global limit enforces autoscale triggers.
nina (Sales): Perfect. Can we get the runbook + quote by EOD tomorrow? Zenith is on a tight procurement cadence.
Olivia (SRE): I'll drop the runbook skeleton into the deal workspace and ping you when done.
Tim (Infra): I'll get pricing ops the model-to-GPU mapping + hourly numbers, ETA tomorrow morning.
Ben (Solutions): I'll prepare the fallback model list and a one-paragraph note on expected quality tradeoffs when using quantized variants.
deploy-bot: runbook-created: deal/zenith/commit-handbook -> https://redwood.internal/notes/zenith-commit-runbook (permission: sales + solutions + infra)
nina (Sales): Awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll loop in legal once we have the runbook.
Olivia (SRE): FYI — add a small test: simulate 12-minute sustained 800 qps window to validate autoscale warms KV cache in our staging. Ben/Tim, can you add that to test matrix?
Ben (Solutions): Yep, I'll add a load test and share results.
Tim (Infra): Added to infra test board.
nina (Sales): Closing notes: deliverables = runbook + two quotes + autoscale policy + short security answers. Thanks all.
